threatFindings.threat: Worker exposure during rebuild can be cut by reordering dependency-safe worker instructions
threatFindings.evidence: Analytic: copy is 2 bytes/turn and execution about 2 bytes/turn, so the summed byte-turn exposure (exec turn - copy turn) is the same under any permutation. Base already puts its 1-byte instructions (stosw, dec di) last and exposes the new anchor for the minimum 2 turns. Screen 8bqu7 (R1): ALL exactly 0, 47/50 cohorts identical.

threatFindings.threat: Rebuild-window deaths scale with the copy-to-exec lag (rep count)
threatFindings.evidence: Trace oyb2n (P7, lag 7) vs base trace pkj3o (lag 9), same 8 cohorts: rebuild-window deaths 41 vs 40 (scratch/A020/phase.cjs). In rebuild deaths the newest foreign fatal byte is <=2 rounds old in 27/46 (base) and 36/50 (P7) cases (scratch/A020/lag.cjs). Only 8/161 base deaths (age 3-20) fit the exposure model; in P7 that bucket was 4. Ceiling about 5% of deaths.
threatFindings.impact: <= ~0.005-0.01 per battle; swamped by trajectory noise

threatFindings.threat: A004 C2's strong-group loss comes from the shorter period
threatFindings.evidence: P7 keeps the period at 275 turns and still lost strong -0.206 (c2qq6); C2 lost -0.163 (ou61i). Both lost most on cohorts sstrong-1/-5, which also swing +-0.3 in other screens (irlaj, q84cd, 956md). The common factor is the changed rebuild trajectory/bytes, not the period.
threatFindings.impact: strong group is chaotic; rebuild-length edits look consistently negative there

recommendation: Do not promote. Close this card: worker instruction reorders are exactly neutral (8bqu7), and the related rep-count shortening is negative even with the period held constant (c2qq6 ALL -0.039 [-0.074,-0.004]). The trace shows rebuild-window deaths are mostly fresh hits, not long-window exposure. Keep the base worker (CX 9, DX 4000h/2400h). One job left unused.
